case_study_insert.main_stem: Solstice Battery Systems (SBS) is a private limited company in the rechargeable battery manufacturing sector, employing a workforce of 50. Founded in 2014 by Priya Solstice, it builds lithium-ion battery packs for forklifts and grid-storage units and operates a hierarchical structure with democratic leadership. SBS plans to invest $940,000 in a battery cell assembly line with an on-site recycling unit, financed by $500,000 venture capital and $440,000 retained profit. It has fixed costs of $320,000 a year, a variable cost of $10.00 a unit and a selling price of $18.00, and currently produces 80,000 units a year. SBS faces two operational problems: a defect rate of 3.1% in cell welding and rising waste from rejected packs.
case_study_insert.appendix_1_marketing_ops: Operations and Waste Report — Q3 2025: The assembly line produced 18,400 battery packs last quarter at a defect rate of 3.1%, down from 4.4% a year earlier. Waste from rejected packs fell from 52 to 33 tonnes a month. Average cycle-test time is 5.4 days. A survey of 410 industrial buyers found 63% would pay up to $0.70 more for recyclable battery packs and 49% check environmental credentials before ordering. Records show 13 of 50 assembly staff have not completed on-the-job training on the welding rigs; recycling-technician courses cost $860 per employee.
case_study_insert.appendix_3_external_environment: Economic and Business Bulletin (November 2026): (1) The central bank has raised the base interest rate from 3.75% to 4.5%, increasing borrowing costs. (2) The national minimum wage will rise by 5.9% from $12.65 to $13.40 an hour from April 2026. (3) Lithium and cobalt input costs have risen 14.2% year-on-year, electricity price inflation is 5.6%, and demand for industrial storage batteries grew 4.0% over the same period.

questions.question_text: SBS plans to raise $500,000 of venture capital for its $940,000 assembly line. Explain two advantages for SBS of venture capital over a bank loan.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Venture capital does not require the regular interest and capital repayments of a bank loan, so SBS can direct its $440,000 retained profit and the $500,000 raised into the $940,000 assembly line without adding debt service to $320,000 a year fixed costs. That protects the $8.00 contribution on 80,000 battery packs while the 3.1% welding defect rate is being reduced.

Point 2: A venture capital investor usually brings sector expertise and contacts as well as money, which can help Priya Solstice recruit recycling technicians and reach grid-storage clients for the 63% of 410 surveyed buyers who would pay $0.70 more for recyclable packs. The risk of the new line is shared with the investor rather than borne by SBS alone, and there is no collateral to pledge, unlike a loan secured on the company's assets.

That matters because the 3.1% welding defect rate on 18,400 packs a quarter already wastes materials, and debt service would reduce the cash available for recycling-technician courses at $860 each.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid advantage of venture capital (max 2).
1 mark for each valid advantage of venture capital (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation applied to SBS's funding, contribution and expansion.
Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation applied to SBS's expertise, risk and survey evidence.

questions.question_text: SBS is launching its new recyclable battery packs. Consider advertising in trade journals, sponsoring an energy-storage exhibition, or e-commerce and social media marketing. Which should SBS choose? Justify your recommendation.
questions.model_answer:
Trade journal advertising: Specialist energy and materials-handling magazines reach the industrial buyers SBS supplies and can carry the message that 63% of 410 surveyed buyers would pay $0.70 more for recyclable packs. However, readership is limited and falling, repeat insertions are costly, and print cannot demonstrate the recycling credentials checked by 49%, making returns uncertain for a 50-employee firm funding a $940,000 line.

Energy-storage exhibition sponsorship: A stand lets forklift and grid-storage buyers inspect packs and ask about recycling, directly reaching the 49% who check environmental credentials and helping overcome concern over a 3.1% defect rate. The drawbacks are high stand and travel costs, a short event and a narrow audience, which may not sustain orders at 80,000 units a year.

E-commerce and social media marketing: Targeted online campaigns can show recycling evidence to the 49% who check it and promote the $0.70 premium to the 63% who value it, at a cost per contact far below print or a show. Results build gradually and need digital skills SBS may have to buy in, but campaigns can be scaled and measured against orders while the new line ramps up.

Recommendation: SBS should choose e-commerce and social media marketing. It reaches the surveyed green segment cost-effectively and can be measured against 80,000-unit output. Trade journals are rejected as narrow and declining; the exhibition is rejected as expensive and short-lived. SBS can add a small exhibition presence later once online demand is established.

SBS should track which ads produce orders for recyclable packs against the 4.0% growth in storage-battery demand noted in the bulletin, so the $940,000 line is not over-committed.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies promotional options with limited application to SBS.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Discusses advantages and disadvantages of at least two options in the context of SBS with some judgement.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Evaluates all three options in the context of SBS and recommends e-commerce and social media, explaining why trade journals and the exhibition are rejected.

questions.question_text: SBS's 3.1% defect rate and rising waste are hurting output. Explain two benefits for SBS of democratic leadership in its production teams.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Democratic leadership lets the 50 assembly staff suggest improvements to welding routines, raising job satisfaction through Maslow's social and esteem needs. Operators who help shape the new cell are more likely to flag faults early, cutting the 3.1% defect rate on the 18,400 packs built last quarter and addressing the 13 of 50 staff still awaiting on-the-job training on the welding rigs.

Point 2: Consultation draws on workers' practical knowledge to reduce waste from rejected packs, which fell from 52 to 33 tonnes a month, and generates ideas for the $860 recycling-technician courses. Higher involvement builds commitment to the 49% of buyers who check environmental credentials, protecting the $8.00 contribution on 80,000 packs. Within a hierarchical structure, democratic consultation also softens the distance between Priya Solstice and the shop floor.

Priya Solstice can hold short consultation meetings each shift without disrupting the 5.4-day cycle-test schedule, and recording suggestions makes the link between involvement and lower waste visible to all 50 staff.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid benefit of democratic leadership (max 2).
1 mark for each valid benefit of democratic leadership (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation linked to SBS's defect rate, waste and training.
Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation linked to SBS's credentials, contribution and structure.

questions.question_text: SBS must staff its new welding line. Consider recruiting apprentices or hiring experienced technicians. Which should SBS choose? Justify your decision.
questions.model_answer:
Apprentices: Training apprentices in SBS's own welding methods is cheaper in wages and builds loyalty, and the on-the-job training already used for the 13 of 50 staff shows the firm can develop skills internally. However, apprentices need supervision and time before they can maintain quality on the $940,000 line, while the current 3.1% defect rate and $860 recycling courses demand immediate skill; relying on trainees could raise waste from rejected packs again.

Experienced technicians: Hiring qualified welders brings proven ability to cut the 3.1% defect rate and keep the 18,400 quarterly packs on specification, shortening the 5.4-day cycle-test time. The disadvantages are higher recruitment and wage costs and possible difficulty attracting scarce battery specialists, so the benefit is not costless.

Decision: SBS should choose experienced technicians for the welding line. The technical defect problem needs immediate proven skill and the $940,000 investment cannot wait for trainees; apprentices are rejected for these critical roles because supervision and delay would worsen waste. SBS can recruit apprentices later for supporting roles once the experienced technicians have set welding standards.

To make the decision work, SBS should offer the experienced technicians a clear induction into its recycling and safety procedures and pair them with existing staff during the first quarter, so the 18,400 packs continue to meet specification. It should also use the $860 courses to upgrade the 13 of 50 assembly staff already in post, creating an internal progression route that keeps morale high without relying on trainees for critical welds. In this way the immediate quality problem is solved while the cooperative builds its own skilled base for the future.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Describes apprentice and experienced recruitment with limited application to SBS.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses benefits and drawbacks of one or both options in the context of SBS.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Evaluates both options in the context of SBS and makes a justified decision that rejects apprentices for the critical roles, covering skills, time and defect rate.

questions.question_text: Calculate and explain how SBS's management can use its cost, break-even and productivity data.

sub_parts.model_answer: Formula: Break-even output = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution per unit. Substitution: $320,000 ÷ ($18.00 − $10.00) = $320,000 ÷ $8.00 = 40,000 units. Answer: break-even output is 40,000 units a year.
Formula: Contribution per unit = Selling price − Variable cost per unit. Substitution: $18.00 − $10.00 = $8.00. Answer: contribution per unit is $8.00.

sub_parts.question_text: Explain four ways SBS's management can use this financial data.
sub_parts.model_answer:
1. Compare break-even of 40,000 units with output of 80,000 units: the margin of safety is 40,000 units, cushioning a fall in forklift orders.
2. Use the $8.00 contribution to price the $0.70 recyclable premium and judge whether the $860 technician courses and recycling unit pay for themselves.
3. Test whether contribution on 80,000 units can attract the $500,000 venture capital and service the $320,000 fixed costs before expanding further.
4. Monitor unit cost of $320,000 ÷ 80,000 + $10.00 = $14.00 to detect waste from the 3.1% defect rate and the 14.2% lithium price rise.

questions.model_answer: (i) Break-even output = 40,000 units | (ii) Contribution per unit = $8.00 | (iii) Four contextual uses: margin of safety 40,000 units; recyclable premium pricing; venture-capital viability; and unit-cost benchmarking at $14.00.

working_marks: 1 mark for correct formula and 1 mark for the accurate numerical answer in (i) and (ii); 1 mark for each valid applied use in (iii).

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 2, evaluate SBS's financial position by calculating the current ratio and the acid test ratio for 2024 and 2025. Has SBS's financial position improved? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Calculations:
Current Ratio 2024 = 1.45 : 1
Current Ratio 2025 = 1.61 : 1
Acid Test Ratio 2024 = 0.85 : 1
Acid Test Ratio 2025 = 1.09 : 1

Detailed workings: In 2024 current assets were $180,000 inventories + $200,000 trade receivables + $55,000 cash = $435,000, and $435,000 ÷ $300,000 current liabilities gives the 2024 measure. In 2025 the corresponding assets were $145,000 + $225,000 + $80,000 = $450,000, and $450,000 ÷ $280,000 gives the 2025 measure. For the stock-excluding measure the 2024 numerator is $435,000 − $180,000 = $255,000, and $255,000 ÷ $300,000 = 0.85; in 2025 $450,000 − $145,000 = $305,000 and $305,000 ÷ $280,000 = 1.09.

Evaluation: Liquidity has strengthened. The broad measure rose from 1.45 to 1.61 as current liabilities fell from $300,000 to $280,000 and cash rose from $55,000 to $80,000. More significantly the stock-excluding measure improved from 0.85 to 1.09 as inventories fell from $180,000 to $145,000, so SBS is less reliant on selling packs from stock to meet short-term debts while funding a $940,000 assembly line. However, trade receivables rose from $200,000 to $225,000, tying up cash; if grid-storage clients pay late the gain could be eroded, and lower stock may strain the 5.4-day cycle-test schedule.

Conclusion: SBS's financial position has improved. Both the 2024–2025 measures (1.45 to 1.61 and 0.85 to 1.09) rose and the improvement is not driven by inventory. The main residual risk is higher receivables, so SBS should tighten credit control before further expansion.

With $450,000 of current assets against $280,000 of current liabilities, the buffer is adequate, but SBS should keep the $500,000 venture-capital funds available for any cash shortfall.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: States financial figures or changes without accurate ratio calculations.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Accurately calculates the current and acid test measures for both years with contextual analysis of the trend.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Accurate calculations for both years with detailed evaluation of inventory, receivables and liabilities movements and a justified conclusion on whether SBS's position improved.

questions.question_text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for SBS of adding the on-site recycling unit to its battery line.
questions.model_answer:
Advantage: An on-site recycling unit can reuse material from rejected packs, cutting waste that has fallen from 52 to 33 tonnes a month and reducing the $8.00 contribution lost on faulty packs among 80,000 units. It also supports the 49% of 410 buyers who check environmental credentials and the 63% who would pay $0.70 more for recyclable packs, strengthening the case for the $940,000 investment.

Disadvantage: The recycling unit adds to the $940,000 already committed and lifts fixed costs above $320,000 a year, raising the 40,000-unit break-even if demand weakens. It needs the 13 of 50 staff to complete on-the-job training and $860 recycling-technician courses, and technical problems in handling lithium could interrupt the 5.4-day cycle-test schedule, undermining output of 18,400 packs a quarter.

SBS should phase the recycling unit after the first quarter so its effect on the 3.1% defect rate and on waste of 33 tonnes a month can be measured, protecting the $8.00 contribution on 80,000 packs before further capital is committed.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage of the recycling unit.
1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage of the recycling unit.
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual development linked to SBS's waste, survey and contribution.
Up to 3 marks per point for contextual development linked to SBS's break-even, training and output.

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 3, evaluate how the rise in the base interest rate to 4.5%, the 5.9% minimum wage increase and the 14.2% rise in lithium and cobalt input costs will affect SBS. Which change will have the greatest impact? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Interest rate rise (3.75% to 4.5%): SBS's $940,000 line is funded by $500,000 venture capital and $440,000 retained profit, so the plan carries no bank-loan interest and no direct interest figure can be invented. Higher rates may make venture capitalists seek a larger stake and could slow grid-storage customers' spending, but the effect on SBS is indirect and small compared with its production costs.

Minimum wage increase (5.9%, to $13.40 an hour): SBS employs 50 staff and the rise pushes up wage costs, but the insert gives no hours worked or pay rates, so no annual total is defensible. The correct comparison is productivity: 80,000 units ÷ 50 staff = 1,600 units per worker. If productivity slips, unit labour costs rise and eat into the $8.00 contribution per pack.

Input cost inflation (14.2% lithium and cobalt): The $10.00 variable cost is not decomposed, so only a bound can be stated — if the entire variable cost rose 14.2% it would add 0.142 × $10.00 = $1.42 a unit, about 80,000 × $1.42 = $113,600 a year. Even a partial rise cuts contribution and threatens the 40,000-unit break-even, though the $0.70 recyclable premium accepted by 63% of buyers gives some cover.

Conclusion: The 14.2% rise in lithium and cobalt will have the greatest impact. It hits every one of the 80,000 packs and directly erodes the $8.00 contribution that supports the $940,000 line, whereas the interest effect is indirect with no loan and the wage effect depends on productivity. Material inflation is therefore the largest and least controllable threat.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies the three external changes with limited application to SBS.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses the impact of at least two changes on SBS's costs, financing or revenue in context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Evaluates all three changes in the context of SBS and justifies why input-cost inflation has the greatest impact while the other two are smaller.
